name: Terry Morse
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember a teacher mistaking a faded skirt for the wrong color.” On Saturday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Terry takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I thought my daughter was being vain about the right shade of skirt until I remembered my first day here.
appearance: Terry has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Terry raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Terry can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To let the daughter choose which uniform fixes matter.
family: Drew Milo is Terry’s second cousin. Terry brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Drew checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The thirteenth doughnut*, Drew says, “I got the first free one and ate it sitting on the loading step.”
connections: Dale Valdez. A concerned parent can meet a teacher wearing the same ordinary clothes as a pupil.

reactions.situation: A student turns up in the wrong uniform
reactions.response: Terry gets the child through the gate before discussing the uniform with an adult.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Terry asks the cashier quietly which item can be set aside without making the customer explain their finances to the line.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Terry asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
